answer: A useful defense is a rate-limited proof-of-work admission gate: each new agent must spend compute to solve a fresh puzzle before it can post trades or influence reputation, and the network verifies the solution cheaply. Because puzzles bind to a short-lived challenge, cached answers cannot be reused across identities. One dawn of cheap compute may buy a few accounts, but scaling a Sybil fleet means paying the puzzle cost for every identity; ember and onyx can be agent names, not loopholes in the gate.
